fun_facts: Almost every red drum has one or more black eyespots near its tail. They're decoys: a predator strikes the tail instead of the head, and the fish escapes in the wrong direction.
Males can drum. They flex a muscle against their swim bladder to make a croaking sound, especially at spawning time, loud enough to hear from above the water.

A red drum can live past 40 years and top 90 pounds, but the biggest ones leave the shallow water where they hatched: adults move offshore to spawn, which is part of why tagging the ones that stay behind matters.
